strategy.summary: Trade the breakout after the market goes quiet, flat by the close. Bollinger Bands (2 standard deviations of the last L closes) sitting inside a Keltner Channel (the same average ± a multiple of ATR) mark a squeeze: price is moving less than its usual range. The first close (or touch) outside that quiet range decides the direction: above goes long, below goes short. A stop at the other side of the box or a fixed ATR distance, an optional profit target, and everything closed at the session's last close.
strategy.formula: squeeze when 2 × stdev(close, L) < Keltner width × ATR(L); box = high / low of the squeeze bars

rules.label: Enter
rules.text: A bar is a squeeze bar when the Bollinger Bands over the last L bars fit inside the Keltner Channel. A run of squeeze bars (at least the minimum, never across the open) makes a box: its highest high and lowest low. The box stays live for 1 or 4 bars after the last compression bar (any box width). Close entry: a bar closes outside the box, filled at the next bar's open. Wick entry: a stop order rests at the box edge and fills the moment price trades through it, at the worse of the bar's open and the edge. The first breakout uses up the box, even when a filter blocks the trade (wrong direction, against the EMA(50) trend, a position already open, or the last 30 minutes of the session).

rules.label: Exit
rules.text: Stop at the far side of the box, or 1.5 × ATR(14) from the entry. Optional target at 1 or 2.5 times that risk. Both are live inside each bar; a bar touching both counts as the stop. Anything still open is closed at the session's last close.

rules.label: Size
rules.text: Long only or both ways; one position at a time, never held overnight. As many whole CL contracts as the account covers at full contract value (no leverage), starting from $1,000,000.

strategy.length_note: All lengths are in bars of the chosen bar size; the minimum box width is in ATR(14).

funnel.name: Start
funnel.why: All 3,840 versions backtested once on 2018–2022 data.

funnel.name: 1 · Integrity
funnel.why: Per-trade checks on every version: the box came only from earlier bars, the breakout was the squeeze's first, fills were never better than the market, nothing was held overnight. Plus 40 random versions re-run on cut-off data. 0 failed.

funnel.name: 2 · Enough trades
funnel.why: Needs ≥100 completed trades and ≥10 a year in ≥4 of the 5 years. Removed 504 (504 on 15min).

funnel.name: 3 · Profit
funnel.why: Needs a net profit, Sharpe ≥ 0.75 and drawdown no worse than 30%. Removed 3,248 (3,248 on 15min); 1,894 of them lost money.

funnel.name: 4 · Stable settings
funnel.why: Each setting is nudged one at a time, down and up: squeeze length, minimum squeeze bars and setup expiry by ±20% (rounded, at least one bar), Keltner width by ±0.25, an ATR stop by ±0.25, the target by ±0.5R and the minimum box width by ±0.25 ATR (the box stop and "no target" have nothing to nudge). At least 70% of the nudged versions must be profitable, with median Sharpe ≥ 0.5. Removed 8.

funnel.name: 6 · Remove duplicates
funnel.why: Versions whose monthly returns correlate ≥ 0.8 form a group; the best 2 of each go on (a group of one keeps its one). 80 versions formed 27 groups; 50 of the 50 picks are distinct backtests.

funnel.name: 8 · Validation
funnel.why: Frozen finalists run once on unseen data: needs net > 0, Sharpe ≥ 0.3, drawdown no worse than 30% and ≥40 trades.

luck.method: Per bar size and direction setting: random intraday trades on random sessions at random times, never overlapping and always closed by the session's last bar, covering the target share of the validation window's bars. Trade lengths are drawn from that group's own validation trades; each trade is long with the group's actual long share (1.0 for long-only, 0.0 for short-only), else short. Same fills, slippage, commission and whole-contract sizing as the strategy; scored with the same daily-Sharpe and time-in-market code.
luck.text: For every whole-percent time in market in each group's 2023–2024 range, 100 random runs trade CL at random times on random days. Each group is one bar size and direction setting. Like the strategy, the random trades are intraday only, never overlap, and are always closed by the session's last bar. Their lengths are drawn from that group's own finalist trades, so trade counts and costs match. Long-only groups trade long and short-only groups short; long-and-short groups go long with the same share of trades their finalists did. They pay the same costs and use the same sizing and Sharpe math as the strategy.

assumptions: Data: Databento CME continuous front month (CL.v.0), 1-minute bars aggregated to 15 minutes. Rolls are back-adjusted so the roll gap is not treated as a price move; the box, stop and target are point distances, so the adjustment does not change them.
Day session only: NYMEX crude day session 09:00-14:30 NY (settlement window) on NYSE trading days. Overnight Globex trading is not used and nothing is held overnight.
Costs: 1 tick slippage per side (stops and wick entries too) and $2.50 commission per contract per side, including the session-close exit.

Indicators (Bollinger, Keltner, ATR, EMA, NR) run over the day-session bars across days, so the overnight gap enters the first bars of each session. A squeeze or NR run never carries over from the day before.

Bar data can't order events inside a bar: a bar that touches both the stop and the target counts as the stop, and on a wick entry's own bar only the stop is checked. Both choices make results worse, not better.
Targets fill at the target price with slippage, as if they were market orders at the touch.
Each trade uses the whole account in whole contracts with no leverage, the same as the mean-reversion and noise-band runs; the stop changes where the trade exits, not how big it is.
Sharpe uses daily mark-to-market returns (√252), with idle cash earning 0%. Time in market is the share of bars with an open position.
Holdout (2025 onward) has not been run. It is a one-time final test and needs an explicit go-ahead.
